findings.title: Data race on `totalBatchesIndexed` and `err` in concurrent goroutines
findings.body: Inside `searchSupport.init()`, the `group.Go` closures concurrently increment `totalBatchesIndexed` (line 189) and assign to the outer `err` variable (line 190) without synchronization. Since `group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers)` allows multiple goroutines to run in parallel, both of these are data races (undefined behavior in Go). The `err` race is especially dangerous: multiple goroutines write to the same variable, and although `group.Wait()` returns the first error independently, the shared `err` is still being raced on. `totalBatchesIndexed` should use `atomic.Int64` or be collected after `group.Wait()`, and the inner `err` should be a local variable (use `:=` or a new declaration) rather than assigning to the outer `err`.

findings.title: Removing the lock from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds for the same key, risking file-index conflicts
findings.body: The old code held `cacheMu` for the entire `BuildIndex` call, which serialized all index builds and prevented two goroutines from building the same key simultaneously. The new code only locks around the final cache write. If two goroutines call `getOrCreateIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` concurrently (e.g., two search requests for a namespace not yet indexed), both will see `nil` from `GetIndex`, both will call `BuildIndex`, and for file-based indexes (`size > FileThreshold`) both will call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory. `bleve.New` returns an error if the path already exists, causing one of the requests to fail. A per-key lock or a `singleflight`-style mechanism is needed to prevent duplicate concurrent builds for the same key.

findings.title: TotalDocs() iterates cache map without holding the read lock
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` ranges over `b.cache` without acquiring `cacheMu.RLock()`. Since `BuildIndex` writes to `b.cache` (now with only a brief lock around the write), concurrent calls to `TotalDocs` and `BuildIndex` constitute a data race on the map. This is a pre-existing issue but is made more likely to trigger by this PR's change to finer-grained locking, which increases the window during which `BuildIndex` can be called concurrently. Adding `b.cacheMu.RLock()`/`RUnlock()` around the iteration would fix it.

findings.title: Integration test unconditionally skipped for postgres
findings.body: The test `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` now skips all postgres runs with a TODO comment. Since the PR moves initialization to startup (a significant behavioral change), losing postgres coverage for the storage server module increases the risk of undetected regressions in that database backend. The skip should be temporary and tracked, or the root cause should be fixed before merging.
